messages:
sophia: heads-up: new onboarding run for orpheus-13b-int4v3 with extended-prefill (40k). saw a repeatable checksum split when switching from oracle prefill -> live inflight at ~18,432 tokens. not a random seed issue.

ben: thanks. can you share the exact flags and smallest failing prefix?

sophia: minimal repro I used:
```
./onboard.sh --model orpheus-13b --quant int4v3 --context 40960 --prefill oracle-to-inflight --seed 7 --kv-debug=trace
```
Log lines:
```
[2026-03-22 09:04:02] prefill.mode=oracle-to-inflight prefill.len=40960
[2026-03-22 09:04:34] kv.checksum(oracle)=0x9f2c11a1
[2026-03-22 09:04:34] kv.checksum(live)=0x9f2c10b5  <-- divergence @ token 18432
```
This reproduces when running on two different machines and with two different tokenizers (BPE vs SentencePiece).

kai: 18,432 = 0x4800, suspiciously aligned with our KV tile size boundary. did you inspect ropestate and kvsync traces?

sophia: posted ropestate dump and kvsync events to the artifact: https://artifacts.redwood/eng-ml/13999/ (see files ropestate.txt, kvsync.log). Key observation: ropestate.phase_accum shows a tiny offset (few units) right after the tile flush event.

mira: could be phase rescaling rounding in int4 path. clock-wrap fix branch touched the rescale math. try ROPE_SCALE_MODE=continuous vs discrete and rerun. also try setting QUANT_ROUND_MODE=floor to see if rounding direction changes outcome.

ben: add a run with FP16 runtime (no int4 kernels) to rule out quant math. if fp16 matches oracle then quant path is likely culprit.

sophia: launching three CI runs: 1) ROPE_SCALE_MODE=continuous, 2) QUANT_ROUND_MODE=floor, 3) FP16 fallback. infra-bot queued them.

infra-bot: CI queued: https://ci.redwood/eng-ml/17310 (continuous)
infra-bot: CI queued: https://ci.redwood/eng-ml/17311 (floor)
infra-bot: CI queued: https://ci.redwood/eng-ml/17312 (fp16-fallback)

zoe: quick thought  could be cross-shard handshake ordering. if a tiled-KV flush races with the rotary accumulator update per-shard, a shard may apply a stale phase when resuming. check ordering in kvsync.log for any PTL_DELAY or ACK reorder.

ben: also check prefetch/write stride. try KV_PREFILL_STRIDE=2048 and 8192 to see if divergence point shifts predictably. that helps differentiate memcopy stride off-by-one vs phase warp rounding.

sophia: good idea. I'll add those. also making a tiny unit-test harness that replays the first 19k tokens and assert kv checksums are identical; that'll make local bisect faster than full CI.

kai: if the unit test fails, good candidate for a deterministic bisect: toggling ropestate update ordering and quantize kernel path. we should capture the exact token at the divergence boundary and compare embeddings to see if the model semantics drift immediately or after a few tokens.

sophia: yes, will dump the token window +/- 8 around 18432 plus embedding diffs. posting when available. ETA ~30m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
